law_title: Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954
verbatim_text: Subject to the provisions of this Act,noperson shall take anypartin thepublicationof anyadvertisementreferringto anydrugin terms which suggest or arecalculated tolead to the use of thatdrugfor,— in women;or (b sexualpleasure;or C) thecorrectionofmenstrual disorderinwomen;or (p)]g the diagnosis,cure,mitigation,treatment or prevention of any disease, disorderorconditionspecifiedintheSchedule,oranyotherdisease, disorder or condition (by whatsoever name called)whichmaybe specified in therulesmadeunder thisAct:
summary: No one may take part in publishing an advertisement that suggests a drug be used for miscarriage or preventing conception in women, for keeping up or improving sexual capacity or pleasure, for correcting menstrual disorders, or to diagnose, cure, mitigate, treat or prevent any disease or condition listed in the Schedule or in the rules.
exceptions: s14: does not apply to a treatise or book dealing with the s3 matters from a bona fide scientific or social standpoint
s14: does not apply to an advertisement relating to a drug sent confidentially, in the prescribed manner, only to a registered medical practitioner
s14: does not apply to an advertisement relating to a drug printed or published with the previous sanction of the Government

s15: the Central Government may by notification exempt specified drugs or classes of drug advertisements from ss3-6 (e.g. Government-approved contraceptives; information-only leaflets and journal ads aimed at registered medical practitioners, if the claims are not false or misleading)

consequence.penalty: Under s7, a first conviction can bring imprisonment of up to six months, or a fine, or both. A later conviction can bring imprisonment of up to one year, or a fine, or both.

law_title: Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954
summary: A person who practises, or claims to practise, administering magic remedies (talismans, mantras, kavachas or other charms) may not take part in publishing an advertisement claiming that such a remedy works for any purpose listed in Section 3, such as Schedule diseases, sexual capacity, menstrual disorders, miscarriage or preventing conception.
exceptions: s14: does not apply to a treatise or book dealing with the s3 matters from a bona fide scientific or social standpoint

s15: the Central Government may by notification exempt specified drugs or classes of drug advertisements from ss3-6 (e.g. Government-approved contraceptives; information-only leaflets and journal ads aimed at registered medical practitioners, if the claims are not false or misleading)

consequence.penalty: Under s7, a first conviction can bring imprisonment of up to six months, or a fine, or both. A later conviction can bring imprisonment of up to one year, or a fine, or both.
